claims.claim: shRNA-mediated knockdown of SOX4 in MDA-MB-231 cells resulted in a decrease of EDN1 expression.
claims.source: In accordance, shRNA-mediated knockdown of SOX4 in MDA-MB-231 cells resulted in a decrease of EDN1 expression (Figure 6A–B, Figure 6—figure supplement 1A–B) and a concomitant decrease in the ability to induce migration and sprouting of endothelial cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 1G–H).
claims.evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR and functional assay data shown in the referenced figures.

claims.claim: A significant increase in sprouting from the SIV was observed in 4-OHT treated ERSOX4 HMLE cells compared to untreated ERSOX4 HMLE cells.
claims.source: A significant increase in sprouting from the SIV was observed in 4-OHT treated ERSOX4 HMLE cells compared to untreated ERSOX4 HMLE cells as well as both treated and untreated ER-control HMLE cells, indicating that conditional activation of SOX4 in HMLE cells can induce angiogenesis in vivo (Figure 5B–D).
claims.evidence: This is supported by zebrafish xenograft data shown in Figure 5B–D.

claims.claim: SOX4-depleted MDA-MB-231 cells were significantly impaired in their ability to induce ectopic sprouting from the SIV.
claims.source: Quantification of neovascularization demonstrated that SOX4-depleted MDA-MB-231 cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B) were significantly impaired in their ability to induce ectopic sprouting from the SIV, as illustrated by a decrease in the number of sprouting vessels and an overall reduction in the percentage of fish with sprouting blood vessels (Figure 5E–G).
claims.evidence: This is supported by zebrafish xenograft data shown in Figure 5E–G.

claims.claim: Depletion of ET-1 in SOX4-activated cells results in the reduction of angiogenic potential.
claims.source: Similar to our previous observations in vitro, depletion of ET-1 in SOX4-activated cells results in the reduction of angiogenic potential, shown by the decreased capacity to induce ectopic sprouting from the SIV (Figure 5H–J).
claims.evidence: This is supported by zebrafish xenograft data shown in Figure 5H–J.

claims.claim: SOX4 controls tumor-induced angiogenesis in vivo, in an ET-1 dependent manner.
claims.source: Taken together, these results indicate that, similar to our in vitro observations, SOX4 controls tumor-induced angiogenesis in vivo, in an ET-1 dependent manner.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the zebrafish xenograft experiments.

claims.claim: Primary tumor growth was unaffected by SOX4 depletion.
claims.source: Prior to injection, we validated the efficiency of SOX4 knockdown by qRT-PCR. This revealed a significant reduction in SOX4 expression in SOX4 KD MDA-MB-231 cells compared to scrambled control cells, which was accompanied by a significant decrease in EDN1 expression (Figure 6A–B). Following validation, cells were transplanted into the mammary fat-pad and we subsequently monitored tumor growth up to six weeks post-implantation. Primary tumor growth was unaffected by SOX4 depletion and both scrambled control and SOX4 KD mice were sacrificed in the same week (Figure 6C).
claims.evidence: This is supported by tumor growth curve data shown in Figure 6C.

claims.claim: SOX4 KD knockdown was maintained in vivo.
claims.source: Analysis of primary tumors by immunohistochemistry (IHC) for SOX4, ET-1 and CD31 (PECAM-1) expression showed that SOX4 KD knockdown was maintained in vivo (Figure 6D).
claims.evidence: This is supported by IHC data shown in Figure 6D.

claims.claim: Quantitative analysis of ET-1 expression revealed a significant reduction in ET-1 IHC staining in SOX4 KD compared to scrambled control tumors.
claims.source: Moreover, quantitative analysis of ET-1 expression revealed a significant reduction in ET-1 IHC staining in SOX4 KD compared to scrambled control tumors (Figure 6D–E).
claims.evidence: This is supported by IHC quantification shown in Figure 6D–E.

claims.claim: SOX4 KD tumors had significantly lower vascularization as illustrated by the reduction in total blood vessel area, blood vessel count and blood vessel size.
claims.source: We next assessed tumor vascularization by quantifying expression of the endothelial cell surface marker CD31. SOX4 KD tumors had significantly lower vascularization as illustrated by the reduction in total blood vessel area, blood vessel count and blood vessel size (Figure 6F).
claims.evidence: This is supported by CD31 quantification shown in Figure 6F.

claims.claim: SOX4 expression is required for tumor-associated ET-1 expression in vivo.
claims.source: These findings demonstrate that SOX4 expression is required for tumor-associated ET-1 expression in vivo, and SOX4-depletion correlates with reduced tumor blood vessel density.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the xenograft mouse model data.

claims.claim: SOX4-depletion correlates with reduced tumor blood vessel density.
claims.source: These findings demonstrate that SOX4 expression is required for tumor-associated ET-1 expression in vivo, and SOX4-depletion correlates with reduced tumor blood vessel density.
claims.evidence: This is supported by CD31 quantification in xenograft tumors.

claims.claim: SOX4 depletion significantly reduced the development of lung metastases.
claims.source: Importantly, SOX4 depletion in this orthotopic xenograft model also significantly reduced the development of lung metastases (Figure 6G).
claims.evidence: This is supported by metastasis quantification shown in Figure 6G.

claims.claim: SOX4 can control multiple aspects of breast tumor biology.
claims.source: Together, these findings demonstrate that SOX4 can control multiple aspects of breast tumor biology, and show for the first time that SOX4 may regulate tumor angiogenesis in vivo.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the xenograft mouse model data showing effects on angiogenesis and metastasis.

claims.claim: Nuclear SOX4 expression was found to significantly correlate with tumor size, histological grade and mitotic index.
claims.source: Nuclear SOX4 expression was found to significantly correlate with tumor size, histological grade and mitotic index, all parameters of poor-prognosis (Figure 7—source data 1, Figure 7—source data 2, Figure 7—source data 3, Figure 7—source data 4, Figure 7—source data 5).
claims.evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of patient TMA data.

claims.claim: High levels of SOX4 expression significantly correlated with decreased overall survival in breast cancer patients.
claims.source: Accordingly, high levels of SOX4 expression significantly correlated with decreased overall survival in breast cancer patients, and this was also observed when patients were subdivided into the major subtypes ILC and IDC (Figure 7C–E).
claims.evidence: This is supported by Kaplan-Meier survival analysis shown in Figure 7C–E.

claims.claim: Patients with high levels of SOX4 have a significantly worse prognosis in the ER-positive tumor group.
claims.source: Stratification of patients with breast cancer according to the ER-status revealed that patients with high levels of SOX4 have a significantly worse prognosis in the ER-positive tumor group, and a trend towards poor-prognosis in the ER-negative tumor group (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A).
claims.evidence: This is supported by survival analysis shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1A.

claims.claim: The percentage of tumors with high SOX4 expression was observed to be significantly higher in those patients who develop metastasis as compared to patients who do not present with metastatic disease.
claims.source: This revealed that the percentage of tumors with high SOX4 expression was observed to be significantly higher in those patients who develop metastasis as compared to patients who do not present with metastatic disease (p=0.016; Figure 7—source data 5).
claims.evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of patient data.

claims.claim: SOX4 expression in the primary tumor reflects the expression level observed in the metastasis.
claims.source: Moreover, analysis of SOX4 expression in 23 matched primary-tumor metastasis patient samples revealed that SOX4 expression in the primary tumor reflects the expression level observed in the metastasis (p=0.039; Figure 7—source data 5).
claims.evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of matched patient samples.

claims.claim: SOX4 expression is a clear marker of poor-prognosis in breast cancer.
claims.source: These observations indicate that SOX4 expression is a clear marker of poor-prognosis in breast cancer and underscore the important role of SOX4 in tumor-progression and metastasis observed in breast cancer model systems.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the patient survival and metastasis data.

claims.claim: No significant benefit to patient survival was observed for adjuvant radio- or chemotherapy-treated SOX4-high tumors as compared to untreated tumors.
claims.source: Interestingly, no significant benefit to patient survival was observed for adjuvant radio- or chemotherapy-treated SOX4-high tumors as compared to untreated tumors, whereas a significant treatment response was observed for SOX4-low tumors (Figure 7—figure supplement 1C).
claims.evidence: This is supported by survival analysis stratified by treatment shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1C.

claims.claim: SOX4 may contribute to therapy resistance.
claims.source: These findings suggest that SOX4 may also contribute to therapy resistance.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the lack of treatment benefit in SOX4-high tumors.

claims.claim: Tumors expressing high levels of SOX4 had a significantly increased total blood vessel area and size.
claims.source: Quantitative analysis of CD34-staining revealed that tumors expressing high levels of SOX4 had a significantly increased total blood vessel area and size, with an apparent but non-significant increase in the total number of blood vessels, thus suggesting that SOX4 can influence tumor-induced angiogenesis in human breast cancer (Figure 7G).
claims.evidence: This is supported by CD34 quantification in patient tumors shown in Figure 7G.

claims.claim: SOX4 can influence tumor-induced angiogenesis in human breast cancer.
claims.source: Quantitative analysis of CD34-staining revealed that tumors expressing high levels of SOX4 had a significantly increased total blood vessel area and size, with an apparent but non-significant increase in the total number of blood vessels, thus suggesting that SOX4 can influence tumor-induced angiogenesis in human breast cancer (Figure 7G).
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the correlation between SOX4 and blood vessel markers in patient tumors.

claims.claim: SOX4 acts as an opportunistic transcription factor directed by a pre-existing chromatin landscape.
claims.source: Our findings indicate that SOX4 acts as an opportunistic transcription factor directed by a pre-existing chromatin landscape, which upon recruitment to open chromatin further enhances the active chromatin-state.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the ChIP-seq data showing SOX4 binding patterns.

claims.claim: Both the specific cell-type epigenome and the expression of co-factors are important in shaping the SOX4 transcriptional network.
claims.source: These observations indicate that both the specific cell-type epigenome and the expression of co-factors are important in shaping the SOX4 transcriptional network, providing an explanation for the relatively minor degree of overlap in SOX4 target genes between cancer-types (Vervoort et al., 2013a).
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the ChIP-seq and motif analysis data.

claims.claim: The SOX4 core-signature is strongly predictive for survival specifically in the Claudinlow breast cancer subtype.
claims.source: An important finding is that the SOX4 core-signature is strongly predictive for survival specifically in the Claudinlow breast cancer subtype.
claims.evidence: This is supported by survival analysis in METABRIC cohort.

claims.claim: Claudinlow breast tumors are characterized by cells that have undergone EMT, have extensive immune cell infiltration and also exhibit activation of the vasculature.
claims.source: Previous studies have identified distinct clusters of genes that distinguish Claudinlow breast cancers from other subtypes. The nature of these gene clusters suggest that Claudinlow breast tumors are characterized by cells that have undergone EMT, have extensive immune cell infiltration and also exhibit activation of the vasculature (Prat and Perou, 2011; Taube et al., 2010; Harrell et al., 2014; Hennessy et al., 2009).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claims.claim: EMT and TGF-β associated genes are significantly enriched in the SOX4 target gene dataset.
claims.source: Accordingly, we find that EMT and TGF-β associated genes are significantly enriched in our SOX4 target gene dataset (Figure 7—figure supplement 2A–B), although major EMT associated transcription factors SNAI1, SNAI2 or TWIST1 were not observed to be regulated (data not shown) (Vervoort et al., 2013a; Tiwari et al., 2013; Zhang et al., 2012).
claims.evidence: This is supported by GSEA analysis shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 2A–B.

claims.claim: The direct transcriptional network of SOX4 is not dependent on the induction of EZH2 in HMLE cells.
claims.source: Despite a previous report that SOX4-mediated induction of EMT occurs through upregulation of EZH2 levels, we did not detect significant regulation of EZH2 upon conditional SOX4 activation in HMLE cells (data not shown). This suggests that the direct transcriptional network of SOX4 is not dependent on the induction of EZH2 in these cells.
claims.evidence: This is based on RNA-seq data not showing EZH2 regulation.

claims.claim: SOX4 may contribute to EMT and the TGF-β response in breast cancer on multiple levels.
claims.source: These findings indicate that SOX4 may contribute to EMT and the TGF-β response in breast cancer on multiple levels.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the enrichment of EMT and TGF-β genes in the SOX4 target dataset.

claims.claim: SOX4-induced tumor angiogenesis may contribute to metastatic dissemination.
claims.source: SOX4-induced tumor angiogenesis may also contribute to metastatic dissemination.
claims.evidence: This is speculated based on the observed effects on angiogenesis and metastasis.

claims.claim: Depletion of SOX4 leads to a reduced number of spontaneous lung metastases in a xenograft model.
claims.source: We have shown that depletion of SOX4 leads to a reduced number of spontaneous lung metastases in a xenograft model, which correlated with decreased ET-1 expression and blood vessel density.
claims.evidence: This is supported by xenograft mouse model data.

claims.claim: Gene signatures associated with vascular activation in Claudinlow tumors were predictive for metastatic dissemination.
claims.source: It has been previously reported that gene signatures associated with vascular activation in Claudinlow tumors were predictive for metastatic dissemination(Harrell et al., 2014).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claims.claim: SOX4-regulated RNAseq data in HMLEs showed enrichment for vascular signatures.
claims.source: Our SOX4-regulated RNAseq data in HMLEs showed enrichment for one of these vascular signatures (Figure 7—figure supplement 2C) suggesting that SOX4 may drive tumor angiogenesis in Claudinlow tumors by regulating these genes in addition to EDN1.
claims.evidence: This is supported by GSEA analysis shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 2C.

claims.claim: ET-1 expression has been demonstrated to positively correlate with tumor-grade and the formation of distant metastasis in breast cancer.
claims.source: In agreement with a role in tumor-progression, ET-1 expression has been demonstrated to positively correlate with tumor-grade and the formation of distant metastasis in breast cancer (Wülfing et al., 2003).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claims.claim: SOX4 induced ET-1 may promote tumor-progression in an autocrine manner by inducing EMT or affecting T-cell infiltration.
claims.source: In addition to promoting angiogenesis, SOX4 induced ET-1 may also promote tumor-progression in an autocrine manner by inducing EMT or for example by affecting T-cell infiltration, both of which have demonstrated in ovarian cancer (Buckanovich et al., 2008; Rosanò et al., 2005; Rosanò et al., 2013).
claims.evidence: This is speculated based on citations to previous work in other cancer types.

claims.claim: Anti-angiogenic therapies targeting the VEGF-receptor pathway have been tested in clinical trials with limited success due to unwanted side-effects.
claims.source: In the last decade a number of anti-angiogenic therapies, mostly targeting the VEGF-receptor pathway, have been tested in clinical trials with limited success due to unwanted side-effects (Jain, 2014).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claims.claim: SOX4 is an interesting therapeutic target in breast cancer, allowing for the simultaneous inhibition of multiple biological processes required for tumor metastasis.
claims.source: As a driver of both EMT and tumor-induced angiogenesis, SOX4 is an interesting therapeutic target in breast cancer, allowing for the simultaneous inhibition of multiple biological processes required for tumor metastasis.
claims.evidence: This is speculated based on the observed functions of SOX4.

claims.claim: ETAR and ETBR receptor inhibitors such as Bosentan are currently used to treat pulmonary vascular hypertension.
claims.source: Alternatively, ETAR and ETBR receptor inhibitors such as Bosentan are currently used to treat pulmonary vascular hypertension, and based on our results could potentially be repurposed to specifically treat aggressive SOX4HI breast tumors (Rosanò et al., 2013).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work and speculation based on current findings.

claims.claim: Promising results were obtained in a number of ovarian cancer patients when ET-1 receptor antagonists were combined with standard chemotherapeutics.
claims.source: Although success of ET-1 receptor antagonists in the treatment of advanced cancers, including glioma and melanoma, has been limited, promising results were obtained in a number of ovarian cancer patients when combined with standard chemotherapeutics (Rosanò et al., 2013).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claims.claim: Patients with SOX4HI tumors are more likely to profit from treatment with ET-1 receptor antagonists.
claims.source: Based on our findings, patients with SOX4HI tumors are more likely to profit from treatment with ET-1 receptor antagonists, thus arguing for the specific monitoring of this subgroup in future clinical studies.
claims.evidence: This is speculated based on the findings showing SOX4 regulates ET-1.

results.result: SOX4 acts as an epigenome-guided transcriptional activator that preferentially binds to regions of active/open chromatin marked by H3K4me3 and H3K27ac, and upon binding, further enhances the active chromatin state by increasing POL2 and H3K27ac occupancy. This binding pattern is context-dependent and varies across different breast cancer cell lines.
results.evaluation: Claims C24-C35 provide comprehensive ChIP-seq evidence showing SOX4 binding enrichment at TSS-proximal sites with active chromatin marks (C25, C28-C30), central enrichment of SOX4 consensus motifs (C26-C27), and increased POL2/H3K27ac upon SOX4 induction (C32). The context-dependency is demonstrated by limited overlap between cell lines (C34). The mechanistic interpretation (C31, C33, C35, C99, C100) is well-supported by the experimental data.

results.result: SOX4 functions predominantly as a transcriptional activator, with 650 core target genes identified through integration of ChIP-seq and RNA-seq data. Of these, 63% are upregulated and only 37% are downregulated, with evidence suggesting that gene repression occurs through indirect secondary mechanisms.
results.evaluation: Claims C36-C42 provide convergent evidence from RNA-seq (C36, C38), ChIP-seq overlap analysis (C37), qRT-PCR validation (C39), GSEA (C40), hypergeometric testing (C41), and quantitative ChIP-seq analysis (C42) all consistently showing SOX4 primarily activates gene expression. The inference about indirect repression (C43) is reasonable given the lack of SOX4 binding enrichment at repressed genes.

results.result: The SOX4 transcriptional network shows breast cancer subtype specificity, with the core SOX4 gene signature strongly predicting poor survival specifically in Claudinlow breast cancers but showing only moderate or no correlation in other subtypes.
results.evaluation: Claims C44-C46 and C101 are supported by survival analysis in the METABRIC cohort showing strong correlation with decreased survival in Claudinlow tumors (C44, C101) but weaker correlations in other subtypes (C45). This provides evidence for context-dependent SOX4 function (C46), consistent with the epigenome-guided mechanism established in the first result.

results.result: The SOX4 transcriptional network is enriched for pro-angiogenic processes, particularly blood vessel morphogenesis, with this association restricted to positively regulated genes including secreted factors involved in angiogenesis.
results.evaluation: Claims C47-C49 are supported by GO-term analysis showing significant enrichment for blood vessel morphogenesis (C47) and secreted angiogenic factors (C48), with this enrichment specific to upregulated genes (C49). This directly supports the abstract claim C4 about pro-angiogenic enrichment and establishes the biological context for the subsequent mechanistic studies.

results.result: SOX4 directly regulates EDN1 expression by binding to a conserved site at -350 bp from the TSS, resulting in increased ET-1 secretion. This regulation is observed across multiple breast cancer cell lines (HMLE, MDA-MB-231, HCC1954).
results.evaluation: Claims C53-C62 provide comprehensive evidence for direct SOX4-EDN1 regulation through multiple complementary approaches: ChIP-seq showing SOX4 binding and increased active marks at the EDN1 locus (C54), RNA-seq and qRT-PCR showing increased EDN1 expression (C54-C55), conservation analysis identifying binding sites (C58), luciferase assays demonstrating the -350 bp site is functional (C59-C60), pull-down assays confirming direct binding (C61), and ELISA showing increased ET-1 secretion (C62). The regulation is validated across multiple cell lines (C56-C57). This strongly supports the abstract claim C5.

results.result: SOX4-induced ET-1 secretion promotes endothelial cell migration, network formation, and sprouting in vitro. These pro-angiogenic effects are mediated through endothelin receptor activation and can be blocked by the receptor antagonist Bosentan or by EDN1 knockdown.
results.evaluation: Claims C63-C76 provide extensive functional validation across three complementary in vitro assays (wound healing, network formation, sprouting). The effects are consistently observed with conditioned media from SOX4-activated cells (C63, C69, C71-C72), can be phenocopied by synthetic ET-1 peptide (C66, C70, C73), are blocked by Bosentan (C64, C72-C73), require EDN1 (C67, C74), and are reversed by SOX4 knockdown (C76). The proliferation control (C65) strengthens the migration interpretation. This comprehensively supports the in vitro component of abstract claim C6.

results.result: SOX4 promotes tumor-induced angiogenesis in vivo in a zebrafish xenograft model in an ET-1-dependent manner, as demonstrated by increased ectopic sprouting from the subintestinal vein upon SOX4 activation and decreased sprouting upon SOX4 or EDN1 depletion.
results.evaluation: Claims C77-C80 provide in vivo validation using zebrafish xenografts showing increased sprouting with SOX4 activation (C77), decreased sprouting with SOX4 knockdown (C78), and rescue by EDN1 depletion (C79). The ET-1 dependence (C80) is well-supported by the EDN1 knockdown experiment. This provides the first in vivo evidence supporting abstract claim C6.

results.result: In an orthotopic mouse xenograft model, SOX4 depletion in MDA-MB-231 cells does not affect primary tumor growth but significantly reduces ET-1 expression, tumor vascularization (blood vessel area, count, and size), and lung metastases.
results.evaluation: Claims C81-C87 provide comprehensive in vivo validation in a clinically relevant mouse model. The lack of effect on primary tumor growth (C81) is clearly stated and documented. The maintained knockdown (C82), reduced ET-1 (C83), decreased vascularization (C84), and reduced metastases (C87) are all well-documented with quantitative IHC analysis. The interpretation (C85-C86, C88) is appropriately cautious about correlation vs. causation. This strongly supports abstract claim C6 for in vivo angiogenesis and extends findings to metastasis.

results.result: In a cohort of 452 breast cancer patients, high nuclear SOX4 expression correlates with poor prognostic parameters (tumor size, histological grade, mitotic index), decreased overall survival across multiple subtypes, increased metastasis, and maintained expression from primary tumor to metastasis.
results.evaluation: Claims C89-C93 provide comprehensive clinical validation through IHC analysis of a large patient cohort (452 patients) with appropriate statistical analyses. The correlations with poor prognostic parameters (C89), decreased survival (C90-C91), metastasis (C92), and matched primary-metastasis samples (C93) are all statistically significant. The interpretation (C94) and abstract claim (C8) are well-supported by this clinical data.

results.result: SOX4-high tumors show no significant survival benefit from adjuvant radio- or chemotherapy compared to untreated tumors, while SOX4-low tumors show significant treatment response, suggesting SOX4 may contribute to therapy resistance.
results.evaluation: Claims C95-C96 are supported by survival analysis stratified by treatment status in the patient cohort. The lack of treatment benefit in SOX4-high tumors versus significant benefit in SOX4-low tumors (C95) provides evidence for the therapy resistance hypothesis (C96). However, this is observational data and the inference about causation is appropriately cautious.

results.result: In human breast tumors, SOX4 expression correlates with increased blood vessel area and size as measured by CD34 staining, suggesting SOX4 influences tumor-induced angiogenesis in human breast cancer.
results.evaluation: Claims C97-C98 are supported by quantitative CD34 IHC analysis in matched SOX4-high and SOX4-low patient tumors (17 each). The significant increase in vessel area and size (C97) supports the inference about SOX4's role in human tumor angiogenesis (C98) and validates abstract claim C7. The non-significant increase in vessel count is appropriately noted.

results.result: The SOX4 target gene dataset shows enrichment for EMT and TGF-β associated genes, though major EMT transcription factors (SNAI1, SNAI2, TWIST1) are not regulated and EZH2 is not significantly induced, suggesting SOX4 contributes to EMT and TGF-β responses through multiple mechanisms independent of EZH2.
results.evaluation: Claims C102-C105 are supported by GSEA analysis showing enrichment for EMT/TGF-β genes (C103) and the observation that EZH2 is not regulated (C104). The interpretation (C105) appropriately reconciles these findings with prior literature (C102) and suggests multiple mechanisms. This provides important mechanistic context for understanding SOX4 function in Claudinlow tumors.

results.result: SOX4-induced tumor angiogenesis may contribute to metastatic dissemination, as SOX4 depletion reduces lung metastases in xenografts and SOX4-regulated genes show enrichment for vascular signatures previously associated with metastasis in Claudinlow tumors.
results.evaluation: Claims C107-C109 provide evidence linking angiogenesis to metastasis through the xenograft data (C107), prior literature on vascular signatures (C108), and GSEA showing enrichment for these signatures in SOX4 targets (C109). However, the speculation about causation (C106) is appropriately cautious as the data cannot definitively separate angiogenesis effects from other SOX4 functions like EMT.

results.result: Background claims establishing SOX4's role in cancer: SOX4 expression is increased in many cancers with context-dependent pro-oncogenic effects, plays roles in development and stem cell populations, correlates with tumor progression and metastasis, promotes EMT and invasion, and shows context-dependent transcriptional networks influenced by cooperating factors.
results.evaluation: Claims C1-C23 are all supported by citations to prior literature (evidence_type: CITATION or KNOWLEDGE). These establish the scientific context and rationale for the current study. While these are not novel findings from this manuscript, they are accurately represented and appropriately cited.

results.result: Discussion claims about therapeutic implications: ET-1 correlates with tumor progression in breast cancer, SOX4 represents an interesting therapeutic target for simultaneously inhibiting EMT and angiogenesis, and ET-1 receptor antagonists like Bosentan could potentially be repurposed for SOX4-high tumors based on prior success in ovarian cancer.
results.evaluation: Claims C110, C112, C115 are supported by citations to prior work. However, claims C111, C113, C114, C116 are speculative (evidence_type: SPECULATION) about therapeutic applications. While these speculations are reasonable based on the presented data, they represent hypotheses for future testing rather than demonstrated results. The therapeutic potential would require clinical validation.
